<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-summary">Summary</button></h2><div id="work-acc-summary" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Abhidhānaratnamālā&quot; is a Sanskrit lexicon that is a comprehensive list of Sanskrit words, arranged alphabetically and divided into several categories based on their meaning and usage.<br><br>The first section of the lexicon deals with nouns, and is further divided into categories such as animals, birds, trees, and minerals. The second section deals with verbs, and includes a wide range of verb forms, tenses, and moods. The third section deals with adjectives, and includes both simple and compound adjectives.<br><br>In addition to these main sections, the &quot;Abhidhānaratnamālā&quot; also includes a variety of supplementary materials, including lists of synonyms and antonyms, examples of usage in poetry and prose, and notes on grammar and syntax. The work is notable for its exhaustive coverage of Sanskrit vocabulary, and is widely regarded as an important resource for scholars and students of Sanskrit language and literature.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contents">Contents</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contents" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">The &quot;Abhidhānaratnamālā&quot; is divided into several sections, each of which focuses on a specific type of word or category of vocabulary. Here is an overview of the contents of each section:<br><br>Nouns (Substantives): This section is divided into several sub-sections, including animals, birds, trees, and minerals. Each sub-section contains a comprehensive list of Sanskrit words related to that category, along with notes on usage and meaning.<br><br>Verbs (Words of Action): This section includes a wide range of verb forms, including present, past, and future tenses, as well as participles, infinitives, and imperatives.<br><br>Adjectives (Words of Qualification): This section includes both simple and compound adjectives, and is divided into sub-sections based on the type of adjective (such as those denoting colour, size, or quality).<br><br>Particles (Words of Connection): This section includes a variety of particles used in Sanskrit grammar, such as conjunctions, prepositions, and adverbs.<br><br>Numbers (Words of Enumeration): This section includes a comprehensive list of Sanskrit numbers, both cardinal and ordinal, as well as fractions and decimals.<br><br>Indeclinables (Words without Declension): This section includes a variety of words that do not change form based on their grammatical role, such as interjections and onomatopoeic words.<br><br>Supplementary Material: This section includes additional resources such as lists of synonyms and antonyms, examples of usage in poetry and prose, and notes on grammar and syntax.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-uniqueness">Uniqueness</button></h2><div id="work-acc-uniqueness" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">&quot;Abhidhānaratnamālā&quot; is unique in several ways. Firstly, it is one of the earliest and most comprehensive Sanskrit lexicons, providing a vast amount of information on the vocabulary and grammar of the language. Secondly, the work is notable for its organization, with words arranged alphabetically and divided into categories based on their meaning and usage. This makes it easy for readers to find the words they are looking for and understand their usage in context. Additionally, the &quot;Abhidhānaratnamālā&quot; includes a wide range of supplementary materials, such as lists of synonyms and antonyms, examples of usage in poetry and prose, and notes on grammar and syntax, which make it a valuable resource for scholars and students of Sanskrit language and literature.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contribution">Contribution &amp; Notes</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contribution" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">&quot;Abhidhānaratnamālā&quot; is considered to be one of the most important and influential works in Sanskrit literature. Its contribution lies in the fact that it is one of the earliest and most comprehensive Sanskrit lexicons, providing a wealth of information on the vocabulary and grammar of the language. The work's organization, with words arranged alphabetically and divided into categories based on their meaning and usage, made it easy for readers to find the words they were looking for and understand their usage in context. The supplementary materials included in the work, such as lists of synonyms and antonyms, examples of usage in poetry and prose, and notes on grammar and syntax, make it a valuable resource for scholars and students of Sanskrit language and literature.<br><br>One notable feature of the &quot;Abhidhānaratnamālā&quot; is its use of examples from various genres of Sanskrit literature, including poetry, drama, and religious texts. This makes the lexicon not only a valuable reference work, but also a window into the wider world of Sanskrit literature and culture. Another interesting aspect of the work is its treatment of technical vocabulary from fields such as medicine, law, and astrology, which provides a glimpse into the specialized knowledge of these fields in ancient India. Additionally, the work includes a number of unusual or rare words that may not be found in other Sanskrit lexicons, making it an important resource for scholars working with specialized or obscure texts. Finally, the &quot;Abhidhānaratnamālā&quot; is notable for its influence on later Sanskrit lexicography, with many subsequent works building on its organization and approach to presenting lexical information.</div></div></div>
